labels.label: rem:minimalite_non_hereditaire

hypotheses.note: U open and closed in M; absolute minimality asked only on some open W ⊇ U

findings: ETT.tex:486, 'quantifying over arbitrarily fine covers of U this forces closure(U) ∩ (M∖U) = ∅' is an argument sketch: no precausality is exhibited, and the transparent-point construction of cexemple:point_transparent needs a boundary point of U with points of U on both sides (it does not apply to U = ]0,+∞[ ⊂ ℝ). Proved: restriction commutes with generation; clopen ⇒ hereditary. The per-precausality reading (P|_U absolutely minimal ⇒ U clopen) is not the paper's intent — it would contradict lem:precausalite_restriction_minimale (ETT.tex:491) — and is formally ruled out by timelikeLine_rules_out_per_precausality_reading.
questions: Subset reading of 'hereditary only for clopen subsets' (ETT.tex:486): for every open, non-clopen U ⊂ M, is there an absolutely minimal precausality on M whose restriction to U is not absolutely minimal? Not stated; open here even for M = ℝ, U = ]0,+∞[ (the transparent-point construction needs a two-sided boundary point).

labels.label: rem:galileo_spacetime_not_strongly

hypotheses.note: n ≥ 1; for n = 0 the remark is false (galileo_zero_stronglyCausal)
as ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ), homeomorphic; general form over ℝ × X with X connected, T1, nontrivial

findings: ETT.tex:273 / 670: Galileo's spacetime R^{n+1} is written with n unrestricted; for n = 0 it is the timelike line, which is strongly causal (galileo_zero_stronglyCausal; also timelikeLine_stronglyCausal in Causal.Lines). The remark holds for n ≥ 1 only.
ETT.tex:274-275: 'p ≤_U q if p ≪_U q or p = q' needs p ∈ U in the second case (relations of a causality on U hold between points of U); carried so.
ETT.tex:672-673: the last sentence (flat model spacetimes are strongly causal) is about the model spaces of subsec:sing_spacetime_defi, absent from the library; not stated.

labels.label: rem:K_neq_I

hypotheses.paper: the other hypotheses of prop:tarentin_fort_K (absolutely minimal, tarentin, second countable Hausdorff, p ∈ Z^-)
hypotheses.note: the witness halfChronoLine satisfies all of them and is causal

findings: ETT.tex:872-875: the conclusion (causal plainness cannot be dropped from prop:tarentin_fort_K) is certified by halfChronoLine (timelike causal relation, chronology only after −1): tarentin, absolutely minimal, causal, 0 ∈ Z^-, not causally plain, ]−∞,−1[ a bubble of J^-(0), −2 ∈ K^-(0) ∖ I^-(0).
ETT.tex:875-877: the BTZ sentence rests on prop:K_calcul and the model space E_0, absent from the library; not stated.
questions: ETT.tex:872-875, the mechanism 'if B is a causal bubble of J^+(p) then B meets K^+(p)': it fails in general (pointedLine: the bubble ]0,+∞[ misses K^+(0) = ∅, bubble_need_not_meet_Kplus), but pointedLine does not satisfy the hypotheses of prop:tarentin_fort_K (not tarentin: J^+(p) = {p} for p ≠ 0, so diamonds near 5 have empty interior; 0 ∉ Z^+ since I^+ = ∅). Under those hypotheses (absolutely minimal, tarentin, p ∈ Z^±) the claim is OPEN. Is it meant under them, and what is its proof?

labels.label: rem:K_plongement_hypotheses

hypotheses.note: M causally plain (prop:tarentin_fort_K is stated and proved for a causally plain M)

findings: ETT.tex:952 'Neither hypothesis can be dispensed with' is certified by two counterexamples: (a) the punctured null plane (ℝ²∖{0}, product order with the null rays through the puncture blocked) is causal, satisfies (b) at every point for both signs, J^-((1,0)) is not closed, and K^-((−1,0)) ⊂ K^-((1,0)), K^+((1,0)) ⊂ K^+((−1,0)) while (−1,0) ≰ (1,0); (b) the spacelike line is causal, satisfies (a), K^± ≡ ∅, and both the order conclusion and injectivity fail.

ETT.tex:323-324 (rem:deux_pushup) and 953: imprecise rather than false. The paper uses 'push-up' for two properties: ETT.tex:290 calls causal plainness 'the push-up property', defi:pushup defines a relational one. With defi:pushup, density of I^-(x) in J^-(x) needs J^-(x) ⊆ Z^- as well (Jminus_subset_closure_Iminus_of_pushUp); without it the spacelike line has defi:pushup (vacuously) and fails density and (b) everywhere (pushUp_does_not_give_hypothesis_b). At ETT.tex:953 the sentence reasons through prop:tarentin_fort_K, so its 'push-up' is causal plainness, which the spacelike line lacks: that sentence is not contradicted. Suggest naming one property per word.
ETT.tex:954 'around which M is causally plain': prop:tarentin_fort_K is for a causally plain M; a local version is not proved anywhere. Certified with global plainness.
ETT.tex:957-958: prop:K_densite_sing belongs to the singular model spaces, absent from the library; not stated.
questions: Is 'around which M is causally plain' (ETT.tex:954) meant as a localisation of prop:tarentin_fort_K? If so it needs its own statement and proof.

kb_proposals: If ≪ is open as a relation on M × M, I^±(p) ⊂ K^±(p) (Causality.Iminus_subset_Kminus): the cheap lower bound for K, no plainness needed.
K^±(p) = ∅ is proved with one sequence u_n → p along which the J^±(u_n) are pairwise disjoint near p: take N from mem_K*_singleton and compare u N, u (N+1).
A counterexample whose claim reads only U = ⊤ can use Causality.ofRelation (global relation restricted to U); disclose that it is not the local causality of the geometric model.
ℝ × X locally connected: no product instance at this pin; for ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) it comes through the normed-space (locally convex) route — import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.LocallyConvex.
